info.tagline: Give every row in a Notion database its own matching icon. Preview first, accept all or one by one.

gallery_listing_info.how_to_use:
1. Open 
   [https://i.allsvgicons.com/notion](https://i.allsvgicons.com/notion)
    and sign in with Google or GitHub.
2. Click Connect Notion and choose the pages or databases to share.
3. Find a page, pick an icon or a cover, check the preview, then click Add to Notion. For a database, open "Whole database", click Preview icons, then accept all or one by one.
gallery_listing_info.description:
All SVG Icons gives your Notion pages icons and covers from a library of 400,000+ SVG icons, brand logos, flags and emoji.

* Set a page icon: search by name or brand, and see it on a preview of your page before you add it.
* Set a cover: pick from 12 illustrated covers, each with a night version.
* Auto-icon a database: every row gets an icon matched to its title. A row called "Stripe" gets the Stripe logo. Notion's bulk edit gives all rows the same icon, and icon sites mean copy and paste per row. Here you see every match first, then accept all or one by one, change a match, or skip a row. Nothing changes until you accept.
* Icon color: keep the original, or pick one of Notion's colors or your own. Logos keep their own colors.
* Undo: put back the previous emoji or linked icon, for one page or a whole run. An image you uploaded to Notion yourself cannot be put back, and the preview warns you before you replace one.

Files are uploaded to your workspace, so they keep working if our service is down. The connection can only see the pages you share with it, and it changes only icons and covers. We keep only an encrypted connection token, its Notion ID and a daily count. Titles are used to match icons and are never saved. We do not store your page content. Undo history stays in your browser, and disconnecting deletes the token.

The free plan includes 50 icons and covers a day. Search and preview are free. Pro removes the daily limit.

info.tagline: Send native product form responses to structured Notion databases.

gallery_listing_info.how_to_use:
1\. Select Add to Notion. If prompted, sign in to Fillo and switch to the Fillo workspace that should own the connection.

2\. In Notion, select one parent page where Fillo may create response databases, then approve access.

3\. Return to Fillo and open the form you want to connect.

4\. Go to Settings → Response destinations → Notion.

5\. Select Create database & enable. Fillo creates a database for that form beneath the page you shared.

6\. Optionally choose which form answer should be used as each Notion page title.

7\. Submit a production-shaped test response and open the new database from Fillo to confirm the mapped properties.



Repeat steps 3–7 for other forms. One workspace connection can serve multiple Fillo forms, and each enabled form receives its own Notion database.
gallery_listing_info.description:
Fillo is headless form infrastructure for product teams. Build forms in the editor or in code and render them natively inside your product—without an iframe.



Connect Notion once, then enable it for any Fillo form. Fillo creates a structured database beneath the Notion page you share during installation. Every accepted response becomes a Notion page with the submission time, Fillo response ID, a Created or Updated label, and properties mapped from the form’s fields.



Use Notion views, filters, assignments, and automations to turn product feedback, customer intake, vendor reviews, applications, and internal requests into work. Choose which answer names each page. When a form gains fields or a Notion property changes, Fillo reconciles the database schema. Delivery failures remain visible in Fillo and can be replayed after the issue is fixed.



Created and updated response events are appended as separate Notion pages, keeping the history explicit. Uploaded files stay in the storage destination selected in Fillo; Notion receives formatted file references rather than file bytes.



Disconnecting Notion stops future deliveries. Existing Notion databases and pages remain in the workspace.
